theme: SCORE against its authors' code and NoGAM against dodiscover on the papers' simulation, z-scored, rescaled, and raw; NOTEARS against its authors' code on the paper's simulation, z-scored, rescaled, and raw; AGES against pcalg on the paper's 10-variable simulation with weak edges
build: SCORE and NoGAM: Andrey pre-release build of 10 November 2026 (version string 0.16.0, the 0.17.0 release branch with score_matching and nogam as merged); cam's records are from the 0.16.0 development build of the screen, on the same datasets | NOTEARS: Andrey pre-release build of 10 November 2026 (version string 0.16.0, the 0.17.0 release branch) | AGES: Andrey pre-release build of 10 November 2026 (version string 0.16.0, the 0.17.0 release branch with ages as merged)
verdict_rule: SCORE and NoGAM: per cell (noise, scale, graph density, variables; 20 datasets): D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(reference) per dataset, on the datasets both fitted; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; the order share (order) is judged the same way with the signs turned, more being better. 10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0). The decision cells are the z-scored and rescaled ones (claim in); the raw cells, where the references read the simulation's units and Andrey standardizes inside its order search, are reported, not judged (claim out). A cell worse on the first seeds (0-19) on either measure was rerun on fresh seeds (20-39, replication), and so was every NoGAM cell better on either measure; SCORE's one cell better on the first seeds (order share) was not rerun. result and order_result are the published verdicts, better or worse only where the fresh seeds agree and a tie otherwise, so a cell better on the first seeds that was not rerun is published as a tie. replicated and order_replicated say which: 'better again', 'better, not repeated', 'better, not rerun', 'tie' (a tie on the first seeds, whatever the fresh seeds gave), 'worse again', or 'worse, not repeated'. pooled is the difference over all 40 seeds of a rerun cell, for information. Floors: SHD against the empty graph's (floor) and the order share against R2-SortnRegress's (order_floor). Floor, in every row that records one (floor): andrey_minus_empty is the 95% interval of the mean of Andrey's error minus the empty estimate's (the empty graph, or for a cause-effect pair a coin flip, 0.5 wrong directions), and reference_minus_empty the same for the reference; the floor applies only where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, where the reference itself beats the empty estimate, and there Andrey's interval must lie wholly below 0 too; elsewhere it is reported as not applied (applies false), with its numbers. The floor is judged on the first seeds; a replication's floor (the rerun on fresh seeds) only confirms a failure there | NOTEARS: per cell (noise, scale, graph, variables; 20 datasets): D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(reference) per dataset, on the datasets both fitted; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise. 10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0). The decision cells are the z-scored ones (claim in), 24: ER2 and SF4, 10 to 100 variables, three noises; the raw cells, where the least-squares fit reads the simulation's units, and the rescaled cells are reported, not judged (claim out), at 10 to 50 variables. No decision cell was worse on the first seeds (0-19), so none was rerun for the comparison with the reference; a cell better on the first seeds was not rerun and is published as a tie. The one decision cell whose floor failed on the first seeds where the reference's passed (SF4, 50 variables, exponential noise) was rerun on fresh seeds, 20-39, and again on 40-59 because the first rerun was worse than the reference on its own seeds; its replication is the 40 fresh datasets pooled, so that no block is selected, with each block of 20 under blocks, and pooled is all 60 datasets. Floor, in every row that records one (floor): andrey_minus_empty is the 95% interval of the mean of Andrey's error minus the empty estimate's (the empty graph, or for a cause-effect pair a coin flip, 0.5 wrong directions), and reference_minus_empty the same for the reference; the floor applies only where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, where the reference itself beats the empty estimate, and there Andrey's interval must lie wholly below 0 too; elsewhere it is reported as not applied (applies false), with its numbers. The floor is judged on the first seeds; a replication's floor (the rerun on fresh seeds) only confirms a failure there | AGES: per setting (strong share, weak share, rows; 20 datasets): D = Andrey - reference per dataset on shd, correct, and wrong; a setting where every dataset has the reference's graph is a tie with every D equal to 0 (same_graph equals paired); otherwise a measure is worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely on its worse side of 0 (above for shd and wrong, below for correct), better when entirely on the other, and the setting is worse if any measure is, better if one is and none is worse, a tie otherwise. mean_D and bootstrap_95 are those of shd. 10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0). A worse setting is rerun on fresh seeds, 20-39, and counts only if it is worse again. Floor, in every row that records one (floor): andrey_minus_empty is the 95% interval of the mean of Andrey's error minus the empty estimate's (the empty graph, or for a cause-effect pair a coin flip, 0.5 wrong directions), and reference_minus_empty the same for the reference; the floor applies only where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, where the reference itself beats the empty estimate, and there Andrey's interval must lie wholly below 0 too; elsewhere it is reported as not applied (applies false), with its numbers. The floor is judged on the first seeds; a replication's floor (the rerun on fresh seeds) only confirms a failure there
card_verdict_rule: card_verdict, on every row: the release card's verdict on the row's comparison, 'better', 'tie', or 'worse', and null where the card judges none (rows out of claim, and rows with fewer than 10 paired datasets). Better or worse counts only where a rerun on fresh seeds agreed; one on the first seeds alone is a tie
fit_protocol: SCORE and NoGAM: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, one timed fit without warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored as a graph; no fit failed or timed out. Andrey's fits, the references' fits, and cam's ran in separate runs on shared nodes, so a time ratio is indicative; ratio is the median over the paired datasets of the reference's time over Andrey's | NOTEARS: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, one timed fit without warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored as a graph; no fit failed or timed out. ratio is the median over the paired datasets of the reference's time over Andrey's, below 1 where Andrey is slower | AGES: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, one untimed warm-up fit then one timed fit, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored as a graph; no fit failed or timed out. ratio is the median over the paired datasets of the reference's time over Andrey's
error_metric: SCORE and NoGAM: SHD of the DAG against the true DAG (a reversed edge counts 1): andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means. The order share is the share of true edges the method's causal order puts in the true direction (the arrowhead recall of the full DAG of the order), 0.5 for a random order on average | NOTEARS: SHD of the DAG against the true DAG (a reversed edge counts 1), the papers' measure: andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means. The _mec_ fields and mec are the SHD between the CPDAGs of the estimate and of the truth, reported and not judged | AGES: shd: the variable pairs where the graph differs from every graph between the true CPDAG and the true DAG (a missing or extra edge, an edge directed against the true DAG, or an edge left undirected that the true CPDAG directs, each 1; an edge directed as the true DAG directs it is no error): andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means. precision is the share of a graph's directed edges that the true DAG directs the same way and recall the share of the true DAG's edges the graph directs correctly, the paper's measures, each pooled over the setting's datasets; measures holds the paired comparison of shd, correct (correctly directed edges) and wrong (other directed edges) with the reference, and against_ges the same against Andrey's GES at the same penalty, with the unshielded colliders of the AGES graph that the GES CPDAG lacks
complete_definition: SCORE and NoGAM: true when every row has at least 10 paired datasets (both fitted) | NOTEARS: true when every row has at least 10 paired datasets (both fitted) | AGES: true when every row has at least 10 paired datasets (both fitted)
seeds_note: SCORE and NoGAM: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19; a replication holds 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39 | NOTEARS: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19; the one replication holds 40 fresh datasets, seeds 20-59 | AGES: every setting holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19; no setting was worse than the reference, so none was rerun

methods.comparator_setting: the SCORE authors' code, github.com/paulrolland1307/SCORE at commit c2c2b8e0, at its defaults (ridge term 0.001, no division of the entries by their mean), its pruning the CAM pruning of the R package with mgcv 1.9-4 at cutoff 0.001, refit with torch 2.13.0+cpu; its results move slightly with the torch version, and the records of the 0.16.0 screen were fit with torch 2.5.1
methods.hardware: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor / AMD EPYC 9534 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; Andrey and the reference ran in separate runs on shared nodes, so the time ratio is indicative and absolute times do not compare across rows
methods.error_metric: SHD of the DAG against the true DAG (a reversed edge counts 1): andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means. The order share is the share of true edges the method's causal order puts in the true direction (the arrowhead recall of the full DAG of the order), 0.5 for a random order on average

methods.error_metric: shd: the variable pairs where the graph differs from every graph between the true CPDAG and the true DAG (a missing or extra edge, an edge directed against the true DAG, or an edge left undirected that the true CPDAG directs, each 1; an edge directed as the true DAG directs it is no error): andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means. precision is the share of a graph's directed edges that the true DAG directs the same way and recall the share of the true DAG's edges the graph directs correctly, the paper's measures, each pooled over the setting's datasets; measures holds the paired comparison of shd, correct (correctly directed edges) and wrong (other directed edges) with the reference, and against_ges the same against Andrey's GES at the same penalty, with the unshielded colliders of the AGES graph that the GES CPDAG lacks
